videoPrompt.description: The COMPLETE prompt for ONE MiniMax H3 generation, written directly as prose against the SKELETON in the instructions -- reproduce that skeleton's headings verbatim, in order, with a blank line between blocks, replacing each bracketed placeholder with your writing. The blocks are: the style/look line (no heading; ONE OR TWO sentences; each attribute stated once; never any hex colour codes); 'Scene overview:'; the storyboard heading; the TIMECODED blocks written literally as '[0s-3.4s]' and tiling the whole duration with no gaps or overlap; 'Camera:'; 'Lighting:'; 'Audio:'; 'Performance:'; and the closing do-not paragraph. Any spoken line goes ON ITS OWN LINE in double quotes inside the timecode block where it is spoken -- never gathered into the audio paragraph (H3 needs to know WHEN the line lands) and never dropped or paraphrased when the scene plan authored one. NEVER write 'Image 1', 'Picture 2', 'reference 3' or any slot number: the renderer prepends its own '<Picture N>' binding clause built from your references array, and a second contradictory numbering is the fastest way to break identity -- re-describe every visible character, object and location BY APPEARANCE instead. Keep the whole thing under ~6000 characters (deliberately not enforced by maxLength -- see the top-level _comment; comfy.minimax_h3_r2v trims to H3's ~7000-char window, prose-first, so the binding clause always survives).

shotStructure.description:
THE DIRECTORIAL DECISION for this scene, made from the beat -- NOT inherited from how many shots the planner budgeted (that number is a duration split). The planner's shots are BEATS; three beats can be one continuous move.
There are THREE values, not two, because 'one continuous take' and 'the camera moves' are separate facts and pretending otherwise produces an incoherent scene -- a take marked continuous with a static camera gets you neither the cut nor any camera work:
  'continuous_moving' = ONE unbroken take in which the CAMERA TRAVELS and does the work a cut would do -- a half-orbit past a shoulder that reveals the second character, a push-in onto a face, an arc that swaps the background behind someone, a rack focus that hands attention across a room. cameraMove MUST name that travel.
  'locked_single'     = ONE unbroken take with a DELIBERATELY STILL camera. Legitimate only when the scene is a SINGLE sustained beat with nothing else that must be seen -- a held portrait, a landscape, one gesture. If the scene needs to show more than one thing and the camera will not move, it is not this.
  'multi_cut'         = two or more shots joined by described cut events.
CHOOSE 'continuous_moving' when: one location, unbroken time, at most two characters, a single escalating emotional beat, physical continuity matters, or intimacy and unbroken truth are the point and a cut would let the audience off the hook.
CHOOSE 'multi_cut' when: scale contrast IS the point, time passes, the location changes, an action has distinct impact beats, comedic timing needs the cut, or you are covering an exchange in shot/reverse. TWO CHARACTERS TALKING IS multi_cut BY DEFAULT -- an exchange has to see both faces, and only a camera that TRAVELS between them earns 'continuous_moving' instead.
CHOOSE 'locked_single' only for a genuine one-beat held shot.

references.description: The reference plates H3 holds identity from for THIS whole scene. ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: subjects first, most important first, and the single `location` reference LAST. HARD CAP 9 (H3's real limit, nearly double LTX MSR's 5) -- but fewer is still better, because every extra plate dilutes the others; cite only what is actually visible somewhere in this scene. Never empty. Appearance STATES are substituted automatically: when a character's ledger state has changed by this scene, the renderer swaps in that state's EDITED plate -- always cite the plain character id, never invent a state id. Because the whole scene renders in ONE pass, a character can only be held from ONE plate here: if their appearance changes mid-scene, cite the state they END in and carry the change itself in the prose.

id.description: MUST exactly match a story_bible id: a `characters` id for type 'character', an `objects` id for type 'object', a `locations` id for type 'location'. An id matching nothing is dropped with a warning and that subject is reinvented from scratch.

type.description: 'character' resolves against the per-character anchor plates (auto-substituted with this scene's appearance-state plate when one exists). 'object' resolves against the per-object anchor plates -- use it only when the scene's action is physically ABOUT that object (held, caught, carried, handed off, dropped). 'location' resolves against the per-location plates and is moved LAST; include exactly one per scene.

appearsAs.description: A SHORT (3-8 word) visual descriptor of what this plate shows, reflecting the character's CURRENT ledger state -- for 'character', stated gender plus one or two defining features ('elderly hunched fisherwoman in a green sari'); for 'object', its current visible state ('cane basket, half full of silver fish'); for 'location', the place and its light ('the fish dock at first light'). The renderer reads this straight into the '<Picture N> -- <appearsAs>' binding clause, so it must read as an identifying description, not a name.

job.description: What this plate is FOR in this scene, as a phrase that completes 'Use it for ___'. This is H3's single highest-leverage instruction -- assigning every reference an explicit job measurably beats handing the model images and a description. Be specific and DIFFERENT per plate: 'the woman's face, build and wardrobe, held identical across every cut' / 'the basket's exact weave, colour and size whenever it is in frame' / 'the location, its architecture, set dressing, palette and light'. Do NOT write a slot number here -- the renderer numbers the plates itself.

duration.description: Seconds this scene runs, 5 to 15. H3 renders 5-15s per call and this whole scene is ONE call, so this is the hard budget every cut has to fit inside -- the renderer clamps anything outside it and snaps the result to H3's 17k+5 frame grid at 24fps, so small deviations are normal. Aim at the section's own budget; if the section's beats genuinely cannot fit in 15 seconds, cut the least essential beat rather than overrunning.

purpose.description: What this scene is FOR in the story -- the single beat it lands.

description: Scene video prompt for MiniMax H3. FIVE fields, deliberately. An earlier version carried fifteen -- styleLine, sceneOverview, camera, lighting, audio, performance, avoid, cameraMove, dialogueLines, beats -- each with its own minLength, and ALSO required videoPrompt to be those same blocks concatenated under literal headings. The per-field minLength was all it bought, and it cost the model writing everything TWICE -- which is exactly what broke. On identical input, deepseek-v4-flash wrote excellent individual fields and then a heading-less run-on videoPrompt, while thinkingcap-27b assembled the headings correctly but wrote thin fields: two models, two different divergences, one root cause. So videoPrompt is now authored DIRECTLY as fill-in-the-blanks prose against the fixed skeleton in prompts/scene_video_prompt.md, and only what the RUNNER consumes (references, duration) or what cannot be recovered from prose (shotStructure, purpose) stays structured. `beats` is gone as well: the timecodes are regexable straight out of the prose, which removes the keep-the-array-in-sync failure entirely. NEVER add maxLength, or a multi-heading `pattern`, anywhere in this file -- both make llama.cpp's JSON-schema-to-GBNF converter emit a grammar it cannot parse, and every structured call then 400s with 'Failed to initialize samplers: failed to parse grammar'.
